exact_items: Keep `route_target` intentionally small and force normalization pressure through `subject_id` and `object_kind/object_id`.
Let specialized contracts carry specialized selectors: `OpenFile` owns `path`, `line`, `range`; `OpenSubject` owns `subject_id` and subject realization rules
Avoid adding a generic nested 'extra args' bag to `route_target`; that would recreate the same drift under a different name.
notes: Contracts_V0.md must own the canonical route_target shape. The key quality bar is restraint — base target object must not grow large.

exact_items: Keep the initial canonical set deliberately small: `doc:<document_id>`, `artifact:<artifact_id>`
Avoid adding `thread:`, `run:`, `wizard:`, `safe_point:`, etc. as `subject_id` families when those are better modeled as `object_kind/object_id`
Declare the initial `subject_id` families narrowly and explicitly.
Declare an early canonical `object_kind` enum family in the contract layer, with room for later controlled extension.
notes: subject_id must stay sparse for openable/renderable content. object_kind covers domain/runtime/governance objects.

exact_items: Cross-owner docs implicated by this seam: Plans/FileManager.md, Plans/storage-plan.md, Plans/FinalGUISpec.md, Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, Plans/Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md
Cross-owner docs implicated: Plans/storage-plan.md, Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md, Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md, Plans/Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md, Plans/FinalGUISpec.md
notes: These docs consume route_target and object_kind/subject_id primitives. They must reference Contracts_V0.md as the owner rather than re-defining navigation semantics locally.

exact_items: `inspector_target` is still useful, but it should stay for reusable detail-pane or subsection focus, not as a universal dumping ground for all feature-local anchors.

Sub-selection is handled by one of three mechanisms: `OpenFile` specialization for `line`/`range`; `inspector_target` for reusable detail-surface focus; object-family-specific anchor fields only when the anchor is truly domain-local and not reusable
Define `inspector_target` narrowly in the contract layer as reusable detail/subsection focus.
notes: inspector_target must stay secondary. wizard_step, message_id, line, range, raw provider fields are NOT inspector_target values.

exact_items: Many current commands and deep-link descriptions still expose raw local IDs directly because there is no normalized target object yet.
Some existing payloads probably carry both context and target in a way that should be split once `route_target` exists.
notes: route_target is referenced by many downstream docs but has no owner contract yet. This is a gap in Contracts_V0.md.
Crosswalk.md also needs a primitive boundary for route-target ownership.
